notes: Vesper OS 1.0 'duskfall' — a complete one-file desktop OS with an evening identity: three themes, six procedural animated wallpapers, synthesized sound design, boot sequence and a lock screen with optional PIN. The window manager supports drag, 8-way resize, edge/corner snapping with previews, minimize-to-dock, maximize, focus/z-order and an alt-tab switcher. A virtual filesystem persisted to localStorage is shared by every app: Files (grid/list, drag-move, Trash with restore, external file import), Terminal (ls/cd/cat/grep/sort/uniq/wc/head/tail/mkdir/rm/mv/cp/tree/find, pipes, > and >> redirection, history, tab completion, neofetch), a text editor with markdown preview and save-as, Easel paint (brush, shapes, flood fill, eyedropper, undo, PNG export into /Pictures), Resonance (three generative Web Audio stations with live visualizer), Comet (asteroids-style game with fixed-timestep physics, touch controls, persistent high score), Pulse monitor, Settings (themes, accents, wallpapers, dock, account, reset), Calculator (shunting-yard, no eval) and Calendar with persisted events. All icons are hand-drawn SVG, all art is canvas/CSS, all audio synthesized at runtime; no external files, fonts or libraries. Tested in Chromium over a static server: boot, unlock, all ten apps, pipes/redirection/completion, save/trash/restore round-trips and theme switching verified with zero console errors. Known limitations: browser localStorage (~5 MB) caps saved images; audio starts on first user gesture per autoplay policy.
